The DAFS Teaching App is a small program that runs on your own laptop and opens
in your web browser. It walks you through the course's Python lessons: you read
a short explanation, write code in an editor, press **Run**, and get feedback
straight away.

This guide shows you how to install it, start it, and keep it up to date.

# What you need

- **Python 3.10 or newer.** Check which version you have by opening a terminal
  (see below) and typing:

  ```bash
  python --version
  ```

  If this prints `Python 3.10` or higher, you're fine. If it prints an older
  version or an error, install Python from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
  or install [Anaconda](https://www.anaconda.com/download) first.

- **A terminal.** This is where you type the commands in this guide.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Windows

Open the Start menu and search for **Anaconda Prompt** (if you installed
Anaconda) or **Command Prompt** (if you installed Python from python.org).

## macOS

Press `Cmd + Space`, type **Terminal**, and press Enter.

## Linux

Open your terminal application (often `Ctrl + Alt + T`).

:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## `python` or `python3`?
On some computers the command is `python3` instead of `python` (and `pip3`
instead of `pip`). If `python --version` doesn't work, try `python3 --version`
and use `python3` / `pip3` everywhere in this guide.
:::

# Installing the app

Copy the command below into your terminal and press Enter:

```bash
pip install https://github.com/JPvdP/dafs-teach/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
```

This downloads the app together with everything it needs (Streamlit, pandas,
NumPy and matplotlib). It can take a minute or two the first time.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Already have Git installed?
You can also install it with Git, which does the same thing:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/JPvdP/dafs-teach.git
```
:::

# Starting the app

In your terminal, type:

```bash
dafs-teach
```

After a few seconds your web browser opens a new tab with the app. If it
doesn't, look in the terminal for a line like
`Local URL: http://localhost:8501` and paste that address into your browser.

::: {.callout-important}
## Keep the terminal open
The terminal window is what runs the app. If you close it, the app stops
working in your browser. When you're done, go back to the terminal and press
`Ctrl + C` to stop the app.
:::

# Using the app

## The first time: enter your name

When you open the app for the first time it asks for your name.

::: {.callout-warning}
Use your **full name exactly as it appears on Brightspace**, and always use
the same spelling. Your completion codes (see below) are linked to this name,
so a typo or a nickname means your codes won't match.
:::

## Working through a lesson

1. On the home page, pick a lesson and click **Open**. Lessons are numbered in
   the order we cover them in class.
2. Read the instructions, then write your code in the editor.
3. Click **▶ Run** to run your code. The app tells you whether your answer
   passes the checks.
4. Stuck? Click **💡 Show hint** to reveal hints one at a time. Use
   **👁 Solution** only as a last resort — you learn far more by trying first.
5. Click **Next →** to go to the next exercise. Use the sidebar to jump between
   exercises, or **← Home** to go back to the list of lessons.

Your progress is saved automatically on your own computer, so you can close
the app and carry on later where you left off.

## Getting your completion code

When you've finished **every** exercise in a lesson, open that lesson's card on
the home page and expand **🎓 Get completion code**. Upload this code to
Brightspace as proof you completed the module.

# Updating the app

New lessons are added during the course. When we announce an update, run:

```bash
pip install --upgrade https://github.com/JPvdP/dafs-teach/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
```

Then start the app again with `dafs-teach`. Your progress is kept.

# Good to know

- **Where is my progress stored?** In a folder called `.dafs_teach` in your
  home folder. Nothing about you is uploaded anywhere.
- **Anonymous progress reports.** After a weekly deadline has passed, the app
  may send your instructor an *anonymous* summary of how the class did on that
  week's exercises (for example, how many attempts an exercise took). Your name
  is never included. You'll see a small notice when this happens.
- **Settings from your instructor.** If your instructor asks you to set a
  variable such as `DAFS_TEACH_SECRET` before starting the app, follow their
  instructions exactly. If you haven't been told to, you don't need to do
  anything.

# Troubleshooting

**`dafs-teach: command not found`** (or "not recognized as an internal or
external command")
: The installation worked, but your terminal can't find the command. Start the
  app this way instead:

  ```bash
  python -m dafs_teach
  ```

**`pip: command not found`**
: Use `python -m pip` instead of `pip`, for example:

  ```bash
  python -m pip install https://github.com/JPvdP/dafs-teach/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
  ```

**An error saying Python 3.10 or higher is required**
: Your Python is too old. Install a newer version (see [What you need]) and try
  again.

**The browser shows "Connection refused" or the page stops responding**
: Check that the terminal running `dafs-teach` is still open. If not, start the
  app again.

**Port 8501 is already in use**
: You probably have the app running in another terminal already. Use that one,
  or close it with `Ctrl + C` and start again.

**Something else?**
: Copy the full error message from the terminal and bring it to the lab
  session, or post it on the course forum on Brightspace.
